quote: I mean, like, you know, you got a bright sunny day and you get only 25% or 30%. You don't get anything lower in the percentage of, producing electricity.
stewart_read: The customer is actively monitoring his system's production percentage and has trimmed a tree specifically to improve sun exposure — this is an engaged, detail-tracking existing customer, a strong profile for a battery or expansion upsell.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as pure confusion/complaint rather than engagement, but the level of specificity (18%, tree-trimming, time-of-day observations) shows genuine ongoing interest rather than a one-off gripe.
coaching_implication: Reps should recognize highly-engaged existing customers like this and lean into cross-sell (which this rep eventually did) rather than treating the call as purely a complaint to defuse.

quote: I know I got a tree in front, but since then, I have trimmed the tree, so it'll get more sunlight.
stewart_read: Customer proactively improved his own system's conditions (tree trimming for more sun), indicating investment in maximizing solar performance — a qualified, motivated existing customer.
coaching_implication: This detail should be logged for the specialist follow-up call as a positive signal — this customer takes action to optimize his system and is a good candidate for further product conversations.

quote: Yeah. I honestly wouldn't know. I'm not really sure what's being used in the home other than what you told me or, like, the production on those days.
stewart_read: Rep admits and recovers with transparency rather than fabricating an explanation — the coaching-favorable version of a knowledge gap.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as a dodge, but there's no redirect attempt here — the rep states the limit plainly, which is the transparent-admission pattern, not evasion.
coaching_implication: This is the right instinct (don't fabricate), but the rep should have offered a concrete next step at this moment — e.g., 'let me have someone pull your actual usage data' — instead of leaving the question fully open until the battery pivot five exchanges later.

quote: Have you considered looking into a battery backup system to store energy yourself rather than relying on ComEd for that?
stewart_read: Rep introduces a specific numeric claim about ComEd's buyback rate ('they're only giving you, like, 70 back' on 100 kWh given) to motivate the battery pitch — this number is not sourced from the customer's own bill or verified data, it's presented as a general utility fact.
alternative_hypothesis: The 70% figure could be an accurate, standard ComEd net-metering rate the rep is trained on, in which case it's legitimate program knowledge, not fabrication.
coaching_implication: Manager should verify whether the 70% buyback figure is a documented, accurate ComEd rate the rep is authorized to cite. If it's an approximation, coach the rep to frame it as illustrative rather than stated as fact to the customer.

quote: Yeah. Absolutely. And, Tay, he'll have all the answers to your questions, and he'll be able to kinda walk you through it step by step.
stewart_read: The callback is booked specifically to resolve the customer's original, unanswered production/banking question plus the new battery interest — the specialist is walking into a call with two open threads, not just a clean battery pitch.
coaching_implication: The handoff needs to explicitly carry forward the original technical question (why production doesn't drop below ~15-18%) so Tate doesn't just pitch the battery cold without addressing what the customer actually asked first.

quote: Is there a good time Tuesday that would work for you for him to give you a call or would make it a good day be better? If that's the fifth.
stewart_read: Rep locks a specific day and confirms a specific time (11 AM) with the customer, which is good booking mechanics for a callback even though this isn't a standard setter button-up.
coaching_implication: This is a positive mechanic worth reinforcing — the rep didn't leave the callback vague ('we'll touch base'), he nailed down day and time on the call.

quote: K. Sounds good, mister Bennett. Appreciate your time. And, yeah, any other questions about the percentage is too, feel free to ask Tate about that. He'll have he might help you out there as well.
stewart_read: The rep closes by casually punting the still-unresolved original percentage question to Tate ('feel free to ask Tate about that') rather than explicitly confirming he'll brief Tate on it himself — the resolution of the customer's actual question is left to chance/customer-initiative rather than owned by the rep.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as sufficient since the callback is already booked and the customer seems satisfied — the exit isn't unanchored in the appointment sense (day/time are locked), only in the sense of not confirming who owns briefing the specialist.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to say something like 'I'll flag your production question for Tate so he has context before he calls' rather than leaving it as an open invitation for the customer to re-ask.
